messages:
katie (eng-platform): kicking off RFC + playbook draft for customer-managed connectivity for private deployments (VPN / BGP migration / static-route fallbacks). pls review: https://docs.internal/redwood/private-connectivity-playbook (draft). looking for quick runs on acceptance criteria, edge cases, and rollout steps. @ravi @mike @olga @jessica

ravi (neteng): :eyes: skimming now. one quick thing — do we expect customers to run a BGP speaker or just provide static routes? the doc seems to assume both but we should call out fallback behavior explicitly.

mike (infra): short note: rollout needs a canary path. propose: 1 tenant on dedicated edge, verify prefix announcement + health checks for 24h, then expand. we should also define metrics: route convergence, packet loss, tail latency for RPCs.

olga (security): important — include KMS/HSM integration checklist and audit log retention for keys and route changes. also TLS cert rotation window and least-privilege ACLs for the control-plane endpoints. add these to acceptance criteria.

katie (eng-platform): thanks — updated doc with a compact acceptance checklist in section 3, pasted below for quick feedback: 

Acceptance criteria (short):
- Customer can establish control-plane connectivity (VPN or BGP) and sign handshake (mutual TLS)
- Egress IP behavior deterministic: either customer-owned public IPs or documented platform SNAT behavior
- Failover: traffic reroutes within N minutes on primary path failure (configurable SLO)
- KMS audit events for key use surfaced to console + logs exported to customer SIEM
- Canary deployment validated: healthy for 24h, <1% error-rate on inference calls, no TLS handshake failures

Edge cases to call out:
- Partial BGP session (one-way routes) -> must fail closed or route to fallback pool?
- IP overlap between customer CIDR and platform control network -> deny and require remediation
- Asymmetric NAT arising from dual-egress paths -> behavioral doc and test steps

Config snippet for reference (BGP peer example):
```
neighbor 203.0.113.10 remote-as 65001
neighbor 203.0.113.10 password <pre-shared>
neighbor 203.0.113.10 ebgp-multihop 2
route-map EXPORT out
  match ip address prefix-list CUSTOMER_PREFIXES
```

We also propose a static-route fallback doc for customers who cannot run BGP.

ravi (neteng): +1 on fallback doc. also suggest adding automation to validate announced prefixes match contract (CIDR whitelist) and simple regexp sanity checks on ASNs. we should add a preflight test that runs from our edge asking customer routes to be announced and verifying them.

mike (infra): question for product/ops — who provides the SNAT IPs during onboarding? options: (A) customer provides public egress IP(s) and we accept them (preferred for compliance) or (B) platform SNATs with our pool and we guarantee sticky mapping. both have pricing/operational impact. @jessica thoughts?

jessica (product): we need to capture SLA implication and pricing in the PRD. if customers want dedicated egress IPs that's an add-on. add acceptance criterion: cost estimate and SKU options for 1/5/10 dedicated IPs. also want a minimal handshake checklist that sales/solutions must complete before kickoff.

ops-bot: doc created: private-connectivity-playbook (draft) by katie. reviewers: ravi, mike, olga, jessica. meeting scheduled: 2025-02-12 16:00 UTC for RFC review.

katie (eng-platform): next steps I suggest: 1) Ravi -> write preflight test and static-route fallback guide (owner) 2) Mike -> define canary telemetry + runbook 3) Olga -> add KMS/HSM and ACL specifics 4) Jessica -> add SLA/pricing rows and handshake checklist. I'll update doc before review meeting and post line-by-line PR. please ack with :thumbsup: and anything missing.

ravi (neteng): 👍 will do, I'll add automation tasks to the sprint board.

mike (infra): 👍 adding telemetry task, will propose alert thresholds.

olga (security): 👍 adding audit + rotation items.

jessica (product): 👍 will draft SLA/pricing rows and handshake.

katie (eng-platform): great — thanks all. if nobody objects I'll lock the doc to review-mode and share a read-only link an hour before the RFC meeting.
